newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEDIUM BELGIAN PAPER BUSY, ELSEWHERE CAUTIOUS.
newsitem.headline: MEDIUM BELGIAN PAPER BUSY, ELSEWHERE CAUTIOUS.

text.p: Active buying in five to 10 year paper was the only feature of an otherwise quiet and flat Belgian linear bond market in morning business on Thursday, and traders spoke of a prevailing mood of caution.
The market appeared to have no momentum of its own, with attention split between the dollar/mark exchange rate and initial August U.S. jobless claims figures due at 1230 GMT.
"There is a small rally in the five years. It is a continuation of yesterday's buying," one trader said.
"But in truth there is not much business, and people are watching the dollar and the U.S. jobless data," he added.
"People were a bit frightened by the downturn. There is a possibility that in the medium term we will return to the highs, but in the meantime people are cautious," another trader said.
"Between the highs and where we are now there are a lot of points where people will take profits," he added.
Traders noted that the yield curve had steepened somewhat after the recent rapid flattening, but ABN-AMRO said in its market commentary that the long term trend was to flatten.
"Therefore we feel that some bouts of steepening should be considered as excellent opportunities to put flatteners on," it said.
Traders also noted that immediate fears of an interest rate rise in Germany seemed to have faded a bit as the dollar failed to breach 1.90 marks, although it remained a background fear.
The one-week repo rate was 3.37/43 percent against 3.41/47 at the opening and 3.49/54 percent late on Wednesday.

At 0915 GMT the yield of the benchmark 10-year OLO was 5.75 percent against Wednesday's closing 5.74, and the spread over Bunds was fluctuating between eight and nine basis points compared with Wednesday's nine.
The front month futures contract was two basis points up at 121.10.
